lease_accounting_convention.convention: OPTION A - leases treated as operating
lease_accounting_convention.statement: Lease principal repayments AND lease interest are fully expensed through the projected owner FCF (lease principal deducted explicitly each year in the FCF build; lease interest already sits inside EBIT via the post-IFRS16 income statement, ahead of the NOPAT tax calculation). Because the full economic cost of the leased fleet is charged through the cash flows, the IFRS16 lease LIABILITY ($373.689m FY2025) is EXCLUDED from net debt in the equity-value bridge. Net debt = bank borrowings only ($258.48m) less cash ($43.261m) = $215.22m. Including the $373.689m lease liability in net debt on top of deducting lease principal from FCF would charge the same lease obligation twice (once as the PV of future payments via the liability, once again as the future payments themselves via the FCF deduction) - this was an error in a prior version of this model, corrected here.
lease_accounting_convention.invariant_check: Each lease dollar is charged exactly once: as a cash outflow in the FCF projection (which is Gordon-capitalized into the terminal value), never again as a balance-sheet liability subtracted from enterprise value.
lease_accounting_convention.rationale_for_option_a_over_b: Freightways' leases (depot/warehouse space, courier vehicles) are genuinely operating in nature - recurring, renewed indefinitely as part of normal operations, not a one-off financing arrangement. Option A (expense through FCF, exclude liability from the bridge) is the cleaner and more standard treatment for an operating lease book of this kind.

valuation_philosophy: Freightways is a premium-multiple, lease-heavy NZ/AU logistics compounder that has never traded below ~19x adjusted P/E or ~2.8x book (and, restated ex-lease-liability, ~7.0-9.0x EV/EBITDA) in 8 years. The single most consequential modelling decision is the treatment of IFRS16 leases: Group EBITDA/EBIT are POST-IFRS16 (lease D&A already added back), and reported cash-flow-statement FCF (OCF minus capex) OMITS the cash cost of the leased fleet, since lease principal repayments sit in FINANCING activities under NZ IFRS16, not operating. This model deducts that lease principal from owner FCF ($57.7m FY2025, cutting owner FCF from a reported $147.7m to a true $88.8m, margin 6.9% vs an 11.5%-implied figure if ignored) - and, having done so, correctly EXCLUDES the IFRS16 lease liability from the net-debt bridge (Option A, see lease_accounting_convention above) so the same lease obligation is not charged a second time as a balance-sheet subtraction. Even after this correction, the DCF still values Freightways materially below both the current price and its historical trading range: base-case intrinsic value is $7.85/share (-43.8%). The residual gap reflects a structural tension the model surfaces rather than resolves: a Gordon-growth perpetuity, discounting the (correctly, now single-counted) thin owner-FCF base at a WACC appropriate for this leveraged, contractor-model-exposed mid-cap (9.5-11% per the specified range), implies a terminal multiple around 5.5-6.2x EV/EBITDA (on a like-for-like ex/incl-lease-liability basis respectively) - below the 10-year historical floor of ~7.0-8.7x. Bridging that gap mechanically would require a WACC near 7.2%, well outside the specified range for a company with net debt/EBITDA ~2.4x and live regulatory risk to its contractor-driver model. This is reported as the model's honest output, not smoothed away: either the market is paying for growth/quality/M&A optionality that a plain Gordon perpetuity structurally cannot capture, or the stock (92nd percentile of its 10-year range) is priced for a lower cost of capital than a leveraged mid-cap arguably warrants. See sanity_check for the full diagnosis.

inputs.net_debt_convention: Bank borrowings ONLY less cash (Option A - excludes IFRS16 lease liability, see lease_accounting_convention block)
inputs.interest_income_strip_rationale: Freightways is a NET DEBT company (net debt $215.2m ex-lease vs FY2025 interest income of only $1.07m); the 'net cash double-count' rule does not apply. Interest income left inside FCF.
inputs.lease_principal_treatment: Group EBITDA/EBIT are POST-IFRS16 (lease D&A already added back inside EBITDA; lease interest sits below EBIT alongside bank interest, inside NOPAT via the tax calc). Cash-flow-statement OCF EXCLUDES the (57.698) lease principal repayment, a financing outflow under NZ IFRS16. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) therefore overstates true owner cash flow by the full lease principal repayment. Owner FCF = reported_fcf - sbc - lease_principal_repayment, applied across FY2022-FY2025 history and all projection years (as % of revenue). CONSISTENCY REQUIREMENT: because this cost is fully expensed through FCF, the lease LIABILITY must be excluded from net debt in the equity bridge - see lease_accounting_convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FRW.NZ_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column (immaterial, $0.35-1.2m/yr, ~0.09-0.1% of revenue; no buybacks, no equity-award tax withholding across 8 years verified)
inputs.uncovered_dilution: immaterial - SBC ~0.1% of revenue, no buybacks, ~0.2-0.4%/yr residual LTI-vesting dilution assumed
inputs.last_complete_fy: FY2025 (year to 30-Jun-2025); FY2026 results due 17-Aug-2026, not yet released

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue-driven component build (NOT equity or blended CAGR)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr/5yr CAGR (13.9%/15.4%) is INFLATED by the August-2022 Allied Express acquisition (FY2022->FY2023 revenue +28.5%) and is NOT organic. EPS 3yr CAGR (1.9%) is depressed by FY2024's cyclical NZ-macro trough. Equity CAGR is distorted by ~13m shares of Allied Express acquisition scrip issued in FY2023. None of the standard CAGR anchors (revenue, EPS, equity) is reliable in isolation for this ticker - the DCF instead uses a revenue-driven component build with an explicit organic-growth-plus-bolt-on-M&A assumption (base case Y1 8.0% decelerating to 4.5% by Y5), calibrated against underlying organic revenue growth (FY2019 +6.0%, FY2020 +2.5%, FY2022 +9.1%, FY2024 +7.8%, FY2025 +6.6% - i.e. non-acquisition years only) rather than the acquisition-inflated blended CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is immaterial for Freightways (~0.1% of revenue) so the SBC-adjusted vs reported FCF CAGR gap is negligible (13.72% vs 13.64% 3yr; 6.21% vs 6.30% 5yr) - SBC is not growing meaningfully faster than cash flow here, unlike SBC-heavy US tech names. The much larger and more consequential adjustment for this ticker is the IFRS16 lease-principal deduction from FCF, paired with excluding the lease liability from net debt (see lease_accounting_convention) - not reflected in these historical CAGRs (computed on SBC-only-adjusted FCF for comparability with the standard methodology) but fully reflected in the DCF's forward owner_fcf build and equity bridge.

base.wc_capture_note: Calibrated to historical FY2022-25 gap between (NOPAT+D&A-capex-lease principal-SBC) and actual reported OCF-based owner FCF, which averaged ~38-41% of YoY revenue change (ex the FY2023 acquisition-distorted year) - reflects real historical working-capital-plus-other-cash-timing drag as the business has scaled, NOT a generic SaaS-style deferred-revenue assumption (Freightways has negative working capital of only ~$45.6m FY2025, mostly contract liabilities/current borrowings, much smaller in proportion than subscription businesses)
base.terminal_cap_multiple_basis: Applied to an EX-LEASE-LIABILITY EV (lease liability separately excluded per the equity bridge convention); see valuation.base.implied_exit_multiple_ev_ebitda_lease_inclusive_equivalent for the like-for-like comparison against the brief's historical (lease-inclusive) multiple table

components.beta_rationale: Moderate cyclicality - Express Package volumes correlate with NZ/AU consumer and business activity, partially offset by the sticky, largely non-cyclical Information Management annuity revenue (~18% of group revenue)
components.capital_weights: Market-cap-weighted using current share price and BANK-DEBT-ONLY net debt (consistent with the Option A lease convention - leases are expensed operationally, not treated as financial leverage for WACC purposes): ~93% equity / ~7% debt
components.regulatory_leverage_premium_rationale: Added for the NZ Employment Relations Amendment Act 2026 contractor-classification 'gateway test' risk to the owner-driver courier model (high-severity regulatory risk per Analysis.json). Balance-sheet leverage premium reduced versus a prior version of this model because, on the Option A convention, financial (bank) leverage is modest (~7% of capital structure) - the larger IFRS16 lease obligation is treated as an operating cost already embedded in the FCF projections, not as financial leverage requiring a separate risk premium.
components.note: Market cap ~NZ$2.5bn (178.8m shares x $13.97) is a stable mid-cap, NOT a micro-cap - no illiquidity premium applied. WACC held within the specified 9.5-11% band; bull case uses 9.0%, bear case uses 11.5% (contractor-reclassification cost shock materializes plus continued NZ macro softness). A diagnostic stress test (see sanity_check) shows the historical EV/EBITDA floor would require WACC near 7.2%, well outside this range - the gap is not a WACC-selection artifact.

valuation.horizon_rationale: EBITDA margin is already stable/mature (18.6-21.4% band over 8 years, FY2025 19.3%) and owner FCF margin path (6.8% -> 8.4% base case) reflects gradual margin-recovery execution already in evidence (Project Evolve pricing, HY26 EBITA margin 13.0%->13.4%) rather than an immature ramp - a 5-year explicit horizon is appropriate per the maturity test (terminal-year margin is not still steeply climbing).

base.exit_multiple_flag: Implied exit EV/EBITDA is 5.54x on the ex-lease-liability EV basis used in this model's equity bridge, or 6.19x when a projected Y5 lease liability ($497.6m, scaled off the FY2025 lease-liability/revenue ratio) is added back for LIKE-FOR-LIKE comparison against the brief's historical multiple table (which is itself computed on a lease-inclusive EV basis - verified by reconciling the brief's FY2024 8.7x and FY2025 10.4x figures against lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA). Both bases sit BELOW the 10-year historical floor of ~8.7x (lease-inclusive) or the ex-lease-restated historical range of ~7.0-9.0x. This is a genuine finding after the lease-double-count fix, not a residual artifact of the fix itself - see sanity_check.diagnosis for the full investigation, including a WACC stress test showing the gap cannot be closed within the specified 9.5-11% WACC range.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC (8%-12%), Columns = terminal growth (1.25%-3.25%). All cells use base-case FCF path, the corrected ex-lease-liability net debt ($215.22m), and the same lower-of-Gordon-vs-11.1x-EV/EBITDA-cap terminal value rule.

sanity_check.note_on_multiples_basis: Historical multiples in the brief's table are SBC-adjusted and computed on a LEASE-INCLUSIVE EV basis (verified by reconciliation: the brief's FY2024 8.7x and FY2025 10.4x EV/EBITDA figures match (price x shares + total-debt-incl-lease - cash) / EBITDA almost exactly, to within rounding). This model's equity bridge now correctly EXCLUDES the lease liability from net debt (Option A convention, see lease_accounting_convention), so implied_exit_multiple_ev_ebitda_exlease is NOT directly comparable to the brief's table without adjustment. implied_exit_multiple_ev_ebitda_lease_inclusive_equivalent adds back a projected Y5 lease liability for a like-for-like comparison.

historical_averages_ex_outlier_fy2021.ev_ebitda_range_exlease_restated: 7.0x (FY2024) - 9.0x (FY2022), reconstructed from bank-debt-only net debt across FY2022-25

sanity_check.double_count_fix_applied: CORRECTED a prior version of this model that subtracted the full IFRS16-inclusive net debt ($588.9m, including the $373.7m lease liability) from enterprise value AFTER ALSO deducting the lease principal repayment from every year of projected owner FCF. That double-counted the same lease obligation (once as a cash-flow deduction feeding the Gordon-capitalized terminal value, once again as a balance-sheet liability subtracted in the bridge). Fixed by excluding the lease liability from net debt (Option A - see lease_accounting_convention), holding enterprise value and the Y5 share count constant: base IV moves from $5.79 to $7.85 (+$2.06/share, +36%). Net debt is now bank borrowings only ($258.48m) less cash ($43.261m) = $215.22m.
sanity_check.diagnosis: After fixing the double-count, base-case implied multiples (P/E 12.9x, P/B 2.1x) remain below the historical ex-outlier averages, and the negative base-case upside (-43.8%) does not trip any of the stated overvaluation thresholds - so no automatic flag fires. HOWEVER, per the coordinator's specific request, this was investigated further rather than accepted at face value: the corrected implied exit EV/EBITDA (5.54x ex-lease, 6.19x lease-inclusive-equivalent) is STILL materially below the 10-year historical floor (8.7x lease-inclusive, ~7.0x ex-lease-restated). Root-caused as follows: (1) it is NOT a residual basis-mismatch artifact of the lease-liability fix - the lease-inclusive-equivalent recalculation (6.19x) still falls below the 7.0-8.7x floor; (2) it is NOT caused by an unreasonably punitive FCF build - the model's Y5 owner-FCF/EBITDA conversion ratio (42.0%) is HIGHER than the FY2025 actual (35.7%), i.e. the model already assumes margin improvement, not stagnation; (3) it IS a mechanical consequence of Gordon-growth capitalizing a genuinely thin owner-FCF base (after the correct, single-counted lease-principal deduction) at a WACC appropriate for this leveraged, contractor-model-exposed mid-cap. A diagnostic stress test shows a WACC near 7.2% (holding terminal growth at 2.25%) would be needed to lift the implied multiple to the 8.7x historical floor - well below the specified 9.5-11% WACC range and arguably too low for a business carrying net debt/EBITDA ~2.4x and live 'gateway test' contractor-reclassification risk. Freightways sits at the 92nd percentile of its 10-year price range on ~25x trailing adjusted P/E; the market's willingness to pay ~7.0-9.0x EV/EBITDA (ex-lease-restated) for this business throughout its history reflects a growth/quality/M&A-optionality premium - a plain Gordon-growth perpetuity, by construction, prices only the steady-state cash flow beyond the explicit 5-year window, not that ongoing option value. The residual gap between DCF and market price is reported as genuine and unresolved, not smoothed away.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Lease-liability double-count REMOVED from the net-debt bridge (see double_count_fix_applied). No other adjustment made to manufacture upside. The remaining gap between intrinsic value and market price, and between the model's implied exit multiple and the historical floor, is reported honestly per the coordinator's explicit instruction not to reach a particular conclusion.
